entry.title: Combined summary - Transaction rate-limiting
entry.summary: The recent update to Bitcoin Core via [pull request 34628](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34628) represents a significant enhancement in the cryptocurrency's network by optimizing transaction handling and CPU utilization. This update is the culmination of a three-year project initiated following an incident that highlighted excessive CPU usage due to slow transaction processing times on a debug-build node. The core issues identified included inefficient iterator implementations by Boost and suboptimal mechanisms dealing with large transaction bursts, which historically amplified outbound transaction data and caused network congestion. The original transaction relay mechanism, designed a decade ago, was intended to manage network loads but has become less effective over time. Changes in transaction patterns, influenced by technological advancements like segregated witness and the increasing use of small text-based inscriptions, have exerted additional strain on this system. In response, developers have removed lingering transactions from per-peer queues and enhanced the processing rate for backlog clearance. A notable strategic shift was the replacement of per-peer queues with a single global queue to consistently reduce CPU load and handle large transaction volumes more efficiently. New bandwidth rate limits were also introduced to prevent node overload during peak periods, aiming to improve network stability and performance. In addition to these technical enhancements, there is an ongoing application of a peer-observer dashboard to monitor node activities effectively. This involves running a node version 31.x alongside several master/v32.0 nodes to facilitate comparison and provide deeper insights into node behavior. This strategy underscores a proactive approach to managing system behaviors and enhancing monitoring processes, reflecting a broader commitment to continual improvement in network management and stability.
